how_many: 71690ab (graphs of d4c2dda): of 17 spellings of a missing value (NA na N/A n/a nan NaN NAN NaT <NA> None null NULL #N/A - . ? unknown), those that convert to a gene (status converted or tie): human 7, mouse 7, pig 8, rhesus 6, cynomolgus 5 (probe p02); HarmonizeFeatures with merge="sum" adds the column nan to SCN11A's feature and NA to XK's, and makes unknown the feature MLH3 (probe p15)
reproducer: reproduce inputs IN-1: human convert("nan"), convert("NA"), convert("NaT"), convert("unknown"); mouse convert("-"), convert("nan"), convert("unknown"); pig convert("N/A"); each with to_release=115
expected: no gene: the strings are pandas' and R's renderings of a missing value (str(float('nan')), R's NA, pandas' NaT), UniProt's placeholder gene name UNKNOWN and placeholders without a letter or digit (truth: the spellings of pandas and R; UniProtKB Gene Name of releases 63 to 78)
got: d4c2dda and 71690ab: human nan -> ENSG00000168356.13 (synonym:case), NA -> ENSG00000047597.7 (synonym:exact), NaT -> ENSG00000204256.16 (synonym:case), unknown -> ENSG00000119684.17 (case); mouse - -> ENSMUSG00000031354.17 (synonym:separator), nan -> a tie of 2 genes, unknown -> a tie of 4 genes; pig N/A -> ENSSSCG00000001527.5 (synonym:exact); status converted or tie
cause: name resolution reads every string as a name: these are real synonyms (HGNC, MGI and EntrezGene synonyms NA, NAN, NAT; UniProt's placeholder UNKNOWN; EntrezGene's "." and pig's "N/A") reached by the exact, case and separator steps; the api refuses only empty and blank strings, and refuses a batch holding a float NaN as a whole, which pushes users to astype(str) and so to "nan"

how_many: 71690ab (graphs of d4c2dda): whole name lists of Ensembl's GTF of release R (primary assembly, one name per gene) inferred as another release: human 5 of 9 releases (55 -> 88, 75 -> 115, 80 -> 84, 105 -> 115, 110 -> 115), mouse 3 of 6 (60 -> 91, 75 -> 115, 110 -> 112); the assembly wrong for the whole name lists of human 75 (GRCh37 -> 38) and mouse 67 (NCBIM37 -> 38); id lists right in every case (probes p06, p10); names of R read as today's synonym, which does not exist at R: human 55 4,851 (11 %), 80 2,261, 105 469; mouse 60 4,147, 110 614 (probe p09)
reproducer: reproduce inputs IN-7: infer_source(<gene names of GTF R>, mode="release") for human R = 55, 75, 80, 105, 110 and mouse R = 60, 75, 110; mode="assembly" for human 75 and mouse 67
expected: release R (the GTF of release R is the list's source); assembly 37 for human 75 (GRCh37) and mouse 67 (NCBIM37) (truth: Ensembl's GTFs)
cause: source inference reads every string at the graph's last release: a symbol renamed after R is read as today's synonym, which exists only after the rename, so every renamed symbol votes for late releases; the margins between releases are a few hundred of 40,000, so these votes decide; for assemblies, a release-75 list's names also exist on GRCh38 and the renamed ones vote there
